collection.title: Web UI component and motion references
collection.intended_use: Reference discovery and pattern analysis; never auto-install from catalogue.

sources.name: NeoBrutalism
observed_claims: Open-code React component library with shadcn CLI registry
Blocks and templates; Figma kit and MCP server support advertised
Neo-brutalist style: thick borders, hard shadows, bold colors, heavy typography, tactile button interactions
risks: Do not assume every block/template is free because free components are advertised.
Review the selected primitive backend and dependencies before installation.
Use the visual style selectively; evaluate readability and brand fit rather than applying it everywhere.

sources.name: SmoothUI
observed_claims: Examples include text effects, interactive cards, buttons, form inputs, notifications and dynamic island-style interactions
Documentation describes reduced-motion support and transform/opacity-oriented animation practices
risks: Measure actual runtime performance rather than assuming marketing performance claims.
Check reduced-motion behaviour in live examples.
Avoid unnecessary animation and bundle weight.

sources.name: Magic UI
observed_claims: Public component documentation lists animated effects, text treatments, grids, cards, buttons, navigation and background patterns
Examples include Animated Beam, Bento Grid, Magic Card, Marquee, Meteors, Orbiting Circles, Shimmer Button, Safari and text animations
risks: Verify current package and component requirements from the live docs.
Review motion intensity, reduced-motion support and mobile performance.
Check whether a desired block/component is free or has separate access terms.

sources.name: Unlumen UI
observed_claims: Animated React components and primitives designed for shadcn projects
Gallery categories include animations, image effects, marketing, navigation, backgrounds/shaders and icons
Gallery labels free and Pro components separately
Examples include hover cards, motion tabs, animated lists, cursor trails, docks, navbars, WebGL backgrounds and SVG icon transitions
risks: Clearly separate free and Pro components in the registry.
Check WebGL/canvas cost and fallback behaviour on low-powered devices.

cross_platform_policy.flutter: These four sources are primarily React/web references. Do not classify their components as Flutter-ready. Extract general UX and visual principles, then implement native Flutter equivalents only when the user task calls for Flutter.
cross_platform_policy.web: Inspect actual component source, framework version, dependencies, accessibility and responsive behaviour before selecting for React/Next.js.
cross_platform_policy.retrieval: Return 2–4 relevant references for a task; prefer matching platform, component role, interaction pattern, licence clarity and evidence confidence.
cross_platform_policy.reuse: Prefer general patterns and original implementation. Copy/install source only after checking the specific component's licence and receiving user approval.

evidence_policy.note: Web metadata is a starting inventory, not a screenshot audit or licence clearance.
